newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Japanese glum about living standards - survey.
newsitem.headline: Japanese glum about living standards - survey.

text.p: Many Japanese believe their standard of living has not improved since their parents' day, a survey of Asian lifestyles reported on Wednesday.
The answers of the Japanese questioned in the 12-nation survey, commissioned by credit card group Mastercard International, contrasted sharply with those of other Asians.
While almost 95 percent of Japanese said they did not enjoy a better living standard than their parents, 85 per cent of Singaporeans and 84 percent of Koreans believed the opposite.
Respondents in Australia, Hong Kong, India, the Philippines and Taiwan also agreed they enjoyed a higher standard of living.
"The Japanese are the most pessimistic, that's fair to say," said Brian Tom, senior vice president of MasterCard, Asia Pacific.

The 'Asian Ideals' lifestyle survey was conducted in June and covered 4,863 people in Australia, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, New Zealand, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan and Thailand.
It identified Singapore as the country most Asians would choose to live in if they could not live in their home nation.
Hong Kong was rated as the top destination for shopping (31 percent) and Australia as the favourite country for intra-Asian tourism (27 percent).
